stem:
Jyoti splits a bean seed and counts two seed leaves (cotyledons). The young plant later shows netted leaf veins and a taproot. In class she learns that two cotyledons mark a dicot and one marks a monocot, and that dicots often have netted veins and a taproot while monocots often have parallel veins and fibrous roots.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Two cotyledons fit a dicot that often shows netted leaf veins.
Two cotyledons fit a dicot that often shows a taproot.
Two cotyledons fit a monocot with parallel leaf veins.
Seed-leaf number has no link to vein pattern or root type.

teacher.key_rationale: Two cotyledons mark a dicot, which typically pairs with netted veins and a taproot. Calling that a monocot reverses the link; saying there is no link omits the connection taught in class.
